lines.text: It has stood for a million years — the Mountain, silent, immense, unbreakable. Switzerland, the nation of the Alps, who defend like the rock itself and never, ever crack.
But across the sands races the Desert Fox — quick, clever, impossible to catch. Tonight, the mountain meets the fox.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-nine. Switzerland, versus Algeria. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
Switzerland arrive as the eternal knockout men — organised, patient, impossible to break. Algeria arrive as the Desert Foxes — champions of Africa, sharp and fearless.
Switzerland — the Mountain. Calm, colossal, and built to outlast anyone.
Granit Xhaka is the captain and the general, running the whole night with iron calm. Breel Embolo is the battering ram who bends defences. And Manuel Akanji strides out of the back like a king.
Ruben Vargas burns down the wing with fearless pace. And Yann Sommer, the veteran wall, makes the impossible look routine.
Algeria — the Desert Foxes. Fast, cunning, and champions of a continent.
Riyad Mahrez, the captain, carries magic in that left foot — one curl and the night changes. Ismaël Bennacer sets the tempo like a metronome. And Amine Gouiri leads the hunt with a killer's calm.
Hicham Boudaoui runs the engine without pause. And Aïssa Mandi holds the line, the wall of the desert.
So here is the riddle. Does the Mountain stand unmoved, as it always has? Or does the Fox find the one path through the rock?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a captain's thunder.
Here is how we see it. Algeria come out racing, quick and clever, and the Mountain is rattled by the speed of the sand.
The Fox strikes first. The whole stadium freezes.
And it lands. Riyad Mahrez curls it into the far corner — pure magic. Algeria lead. The Fox has drawn blood.
But mountains do not move. Switzerland steady, the press tightens, and the weight begins to tell.
And Breel Embolo batters one home. One — one. The Mountain is rumbling now.
And then, late, the thunder. Granit Xhaka arrives and drives it low into the net. Two — one, Switzerland. The Mountain stands.
Two — one. Algeria were brilliant, and fearless, and so nearly there — but the Mountain would not be moved, the way it never is.
Our prediction — Switzerland two, Algeria one. Xhaka, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Algeria leave with their heads high — the Fox that scaled the impossible, undone only in the dying minutes.
Switzerland march on. The Mountain, reminding the world that some things simply do not fall.
So you tell me — the mountain, or the fox? Comment SWITZERLAND for the Mountain — comment ALGERIA for the Desert Foxes.
Above the clouds it has watched forever — granite shoulders, a crown of snow, the silent guardian of the high passes. Legend eighty-nine — the Mountain, Guardian of the Alps.
The players write the night. But the Mountain carries one truth — you do not have to be loud to be unbeatable. You only have to stand.
